title: This Bird Flew for 10 Months Without Landing Once

scenes.text: This bird flew for 10 months without landing once.
The common swift. Scientists tagged 13. Some never touched the ground for ten months.
It eats in the air, drinks in the air, and scientists think it sleeps in the air, gliding.
Every dawn and dusk it climbs two to three kilometres up, then drifts down.
It lands only to breed, about two months a year. Then it's gone again.
A 20 year life adds up to seven round trips to the Moon. On the wing.

description:
Common swifts can stay airborne for ten months straight without landing.
Researchers at Lund University tracked 13 swifts with tiny data loggers; some never landed once in ten months, and the rest spent more than 99.5 percent of that time in the air. The birds climb to two or three kilometres at dawn and dusk and may sleep while gliding. Over a lifetime of up to 20 years, that is about seven round trips to the Moon.
Could you stay off the ground for ten months? Comment below.
first_comment: A swift's legs are so short and weak it can barely walk, which is why it does everything else in the air. If you had to pick: live in the air like a swift or underwater like a whale?
